clue.text: They advocate close-fitting underwear

definitions.meaning: barristers who argue cases, a sense of the word for instructions given to counsel

explanation.surface: A lingerie advertisement whose models are said to champion snug undergarments.
explanation.definitionFit: The plural noun names both lawyers taking cases (in slang) and tight short underpants.

clue.text: Ducks right inside hollow part of boat

parts.note: to bow is to duck one's head

indicators.note: inside places the letter within the word for hollow

parts.note: a pit is a hollow in the ground

explanation.surface: Ducks swim right into the hollow of a boat's hull.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' puts R into PIT to give PRIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A spar projecting forward from a sailing ship's bow is a part of the vessel.

clue.text: Medics find missing wings on seabirds

indicators.note: wings are the outer letters, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: Doctors discover some seabirds that cannot fly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing wings' trims FIND to IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Junior hospital doctors in training, especially in American usage, are medics.

clue.text: Fast insect circling me in sky

parts.note: fast means fixed or secure, as firm does

indicators.note: circling means going round, so the insect's name encloses the small word

parts.note: an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: A quick insect wheels around overhead in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: A poetic word for the heavens, the vault of the sky.

clue.text: Fought little bit with journalist penning page

indicators.note: penning means enclosing, as a pen holds animals, so one piece goes within the others

parts.note: a scrap is a small fragment
ED is short for editor, the stock crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter scribbling on a scrap of paper seems to be in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fought' reads as part of the scene but is the definition, in the sense of had a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrap is informal for to brawl, so its past tense is a synonym of fought.

clue.text: Pulped more sour quince for sandwich

indicators.note: pulped means crushed to a mash, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Mashed tart fruit is spread inside a lunchtime snack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulped' rearranges MORE SOUR QUINCE.
explanation.definitionFit: A French toasted ham and cheese snack between bread is a sandwich.

clue.text: A note in Zulu about ancient person

indicators.note: in places the note between the two letters

parts.note: Z is Zulu in the NATO phonetic alphabet
C is circa, Latin for about
te is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A musical note in the Zulu language about an ancient figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' sets TE between Z and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Mexican people whose empire fell in the sixteenth century is an ancient person.

clue.text: Bother father on toilet, one on the throne

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
lav, short for lavatory, is British slang for toilet
ER, Elizabeth Regina, was a monarch on the British throne

explanation.surface: A fuss as Dad sits on the toilet, crudely called the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface plays on 'throne' as slang for the toilet; here it is the royal seat.
explanation.definitionFit: A fuss or tiresome rigmarole is a bother, as in what a carry-on.

clue.text: Abandon course after losing heart

indicators.note: heart is the central letter, which is dropped

parts.note: dessert is the sweet course of a meal

explanation.surface: Someone gives up on a training course after losing their nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' removes the middle S of DESSERT. 'course' suggests a programme of study, but it is a meal course.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert someone is to leave or forsake them, a synonym of abandon.

clue.text: Husky reportedly on trunk, crazy for trees

indicators.note: reportedly signals a word said, giving its sound-alike spelling

parts.note: a husky voice is a hoarse one
a chest is a trunk for storage, and also the torso
nuts is slang for crazy

explanation.surface: A husky dog strapped to a trunk goes mad among the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husky' looks like the sled dog but means hoarse-voiced.
explanation.definitionFit: Large flowering trees bearing glossy brown conkers, the plural being trees.

clue.text: Might seahorses be required for this sport?

definitions.text: Might seahorses be required for this sport?

parts.words: Might seahorses be required for this sport?
parts.note: polo is played on horseback, so a version in a pool would whimsically need sea creatures for mounts

explanation.surface: A child's question about which aquatic game needs seahorses.
explanation.definitionFit: A team ball game played by swimmers in a pool, named after the equestrian game.

clue.text: Leader in hunt going east for yaks

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word for hunt is the one that travels
in an across answer east is rightwards, so the first letter goes to the end

parts.note: to stalk prey is to hunt it

explanation.surface: A huntsman leading the chase heads east looking for yaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader in' and 'going east' move the S of STALK from the front to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To yak is slang for chattering, so yaks is a verb meaning chats at length.

clue.text: Could be resort hotel agent backed

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the joined pieces are read right to left

parts.note: a spa is a health resort
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a rep, short for representative, acts as an agent

explanation.surface: A travel agent hedges about whether a spa hotel booking might happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' reverses the whole string of pieces, not just the last one.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses possibility, equivalent to maybe or possibly.

clue.text: Reveal a Parisian caught by Kent port not opening

parts.note: un is French for a, as a Parisian would say it
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the first letter of the port is dropped, the opening being the start of the word

parts.note: Dover is the ferry port in the English county of Kent

explanation.surface: A French visitor is detained at a Channel port as the scene unfolds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not opening' removes the D from DOVER, leaving OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: To take the cover off something is to expose or disclose it, a synonym.

clue.text: Itinerant Aussie without a family

indicators.note: an itinerant wanders about, so the letters roam into a new order
the letter a is left out of the pool before it is rearranged

explanation.surface: A wandering Australian traveller has no relatives to speak of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes A from AUSSIE, and 'Itinerant' rearranges the remaining SUSIE.
explanation.definitionFit: In legal and formal usage, offspring or descendants are called one's issue.

clue.text: Approached gathering soft wood for heat source

indicators.note: gathering means taking in, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: came means drew near
P is piano, the musical direction for soft
fir is a softwood timber

explanation.surface: Someone came near collecting kindling to warm themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: An open blaze built outdoors at a camp gives warmth, so it is a source of heat.

clue.text: Grit ruined red outfit

indicators.note: ruined means wrecked, so the letters are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Mud has spoilt someone's scarlet clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruined' rearranges RED OUTFIT. 'Grit' looks like dirt, but means courage.
explanation.definitionFit: Courage and resilience in adversity, which grit also means.

clue.text: Document about device that's used

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the document goes round the scheme

parts.note: a deed is a legal document
a ploy is a device or stratagem

explanation.surface: A legal paper describes a gadget that has been put to use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'device' looks like a gadget but means a trick or scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: Deployed means brought into action or put to use.

clue.text: Way around New Age temple

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for way encloses a letter

parts.note: a path is a way
an eon is an age, an immensely long period

explanation.surface: A path leads round a New Age place of worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts N inside PATH to give PANTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman temple to all the gods, and by extension any shrine, bears this name.

clue.text: On article, grime's upset European

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in a down entry the word reads upwards

parts.note: dirt is grime, and the 's adds an S

explanation.surface: A European is upset by a newspaper article about grime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' is the definition: sitting with a leg on each side, as on a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting with legs either side, as on a horse; it means on top of something in that way.

clue.text: Trip outside good bank

indicators.note: outside means placed around, so the word for trip goes round the letter

parts.note: a ride is a trip or journey

explanation.surface: A trip outdoors to a fine riverside spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps RIDE around G.
explanation.definitionFit: A raised strip of earth or a long elevated crest is a bank.

clue.text: One boring doctor, comparatively sick

parts.note: the comparative form of ill means sicker

explanation.surface: A dull physician seems even sicker than the patients.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' seems to mean dull, but it means making holes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone or something that bores holes, as in an oil-well worker, is one boring.

clue.text: A formal garment on American, time for change

parts.note: DJ, dinner jacket, is a formal garment

explanation.surface: An American in a tuxedo realises it is time to get changed.
explanation.definitionFit: To adjust is to alter or modify slightly, a synonym of change as a verb.

clue.text: Bumbling tired to US city

indicators.note: bumbling means clumsy and muddled, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A weary traveller stumbles their way to an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bumbling' rearranges TIRED and TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Michigan city known for the motor industry is an American city.

clue.text: Love winner knocking out popular title-holder

parts.note: love is a zero score in tennis, shaped like O

indicators.note: knocking out means removing, so letters are taken out of the word

parts.note: taken as written
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A tennis champion knocks out a crowd favourite to keep the title.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocking out' removes IN from WINNER, leaving WNER. 'title-holder' suggests a champion, but it means a property's legal owner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone holding legal title to property possesses it.

clue.text: Original one, Titian lacking frame in the Netherlands

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in places the trimmed painter's name inside the country code

parts.note: NL is the international code for the Netherlands

indicators.note: without its frame the name loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An original Titian, missing its frame, is found in a Dutch collection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Original' is the definition, not a description of the painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Initial means first or at the beginning, so it matches original in that sense.

clue.text: Group swelling after first of barriers is removed

indicators.note: is removed says that letter is taken out of the word for swelling

parts.note: a bunion is a painful swelling on the foot

indicators.note: the opening letter of barriers is the one taken

explanation.surface: After the barricades are cleared, a swelling crowd gathers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first of barriers' gives B; 'is removed' drops it from BUNION.
explanation.definitionFit: An alliance or association of people, such as a trade body, is a group.

clue.text: Burn-out's regularly struck university friend, remarkably

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter is taken

parts.note: an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A burned-out student is surprisingly struck by a university friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of BURN-OUT'S: U, N, U, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Done in an out-of-the-ordinary way, which is what remarkably also conveys.

clue.text: Suppose, taking helium in, to go up

indicators.note: taking means absorbing, so the small word holds the element symbol
in confirms the helium sits inside the small word

parts.note: HE is the chemical symbol for helium
to rise is to go up

explanation.surface: A balloon full of helium is presumed to float upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... in' is split around the element, which sits inside the small word.
explanation.definitionFit: To form a theory is to speculate or hypothesise, a synonym of suppose.

clue.text: Worried characters in cafe are dodgy

indicators.note: characters means letters, so the answer is found among the letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Customers are nervous because the coffee shops look shady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in' finds the letters run across cafE ARE Dodgy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being afraid of something is close to being anxious or worried about it.
